summary: David Whaley recounts finishing The First Tree under extreme time and budget constraints while holding a full-time job, a family, and a partner pursuing art. The talk traces the game’s two intertwined stories, its Steam debut in 2017, and a console port that followed. He explains the core tactics that allowed completion and later growth: leveraging publicly licensed assets and affordable music, adopting a visuals-first, asset-modification approach, and maintaining a daily 1% progress mindset. Marketing was built around consistent GIF-based posts across Reddit, Imgur, Tumblr, and Twitter, with a focus on early assets (website, trailer, Steam page) and data-driven trailer creation using engagement signals. He also covers the costs, revenue milestones, and the lessons learned about scope, quality, and working with partners (Duke Games, DoGames) to port to consoles. The talk culminates with practical tips on authenticity in promotion, building an email/list, and the importance of finishing a project for both personal and financial reasons, followed by a Q&A on refining their approach and platform-specific strategies.
